issues.description: Acceptance criterion 2 is not met: the assign dropdown does not label an expired worker "Expired". templates/shifts.html:26 still renders `<option value="{{ worker.id }}">{{ worker.name }}</option>` for every candidate. assignments.py:36-38 `candidates(scope, shift)` still returns workers without an `expired` flag, and app.py `shifts()` does not pass `clock.today()` to it. patch.implement_output:
Expired workers now appear in the shifts board's assign dropdown labelled "(Expired)" and can't be selected. All four validation commands pass.

**Steps**
1. **`assignments.py`:** added `with_expiry(workers, today)`, which reuses `rules.registration_expired`. `candidates` now takes `today`, returns `with_expiry(...)`, and has the docstring the plan asked for.
2. **`app.py` `shifts()`:** sets `today = clock.today()` and uses it for both `scope.shifts(from_day=today)` and `assignments.candidates(scope, shift, today)`. Nothing else in the file changed.
3. **`templates/shifts.html`:** an expired worker's option renders as `disabled` with " (Expired)" after the name. Options for other workers are unchanged.
4. **`tests/test_journeys.py`:** added `test_expired_worker_is_labelled_and_disabled_in_the_dropdown` after the refusal test. The existing tests are untouched.
5. **`e2e/scenario.py`:** replaced the two old steps (pick Chloe, then submit and get refused) with one step that opens the `#assign-8` dropdown and checks it, saving screenshot `expired-unavailable`. All other steps are unchanged, and `e2e/capture.py` was not edited.
6. **Validation:** all commands pass and no fixes were needed. `e2e-results/` now has `04-expired-unavailable.png`, which shows the open list with "Chloe Martin (Expired)" greyed out and Amara Jones, Daniel Reyes and Sam Okafor selectable. The old `expired-refused` screenshot is no longer there.

No deviations, and nothing needs a human.

**Validation results**

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `python -m pytest -q tests` | PASS (48 passed) |
| `python -m pytest -q tests/test_isolation.py` | PASS (16 passed) |
| `python e2e/capture.py` | PASS (9 steps, 6 screenshots, video) |
| `python -m pytest -q tests/test_journeys.py -k "dropdown or expired" && ls e2e-results/*-expired-unavailable.png` | PASS (4 passed, file exists) |

issues.description: Three tests that the spec names as the proof for its acceptance criteria are missing. (1) tests/test_journeys.py::test_workers_page_marks_only_riverside_expired_worker (Riverside manager sees one badge, on worker-103) is not there. (2) tests/test_journeys.py::test_registration_is_not_expired_on_its_expiry_day (with ROTA_TODAY=2026-02-14 there is no badge and '<option value="3">Chloe Martin</option>' stays enabled) is not there; this is the only proof for the criterion 'On the expiry day itself, nothing is marked'. (3) tests/test_api.py::test_workers_api_shape_is_unchanged is not there; it was to prove that /api/workers keys are unchanged. Only two tests were added: tests/test_journeys.py:39-46 (dropdown) and tests/test_journeys.py:61-67 (Northfield badge, named test_workers_page_marks_expired_registrations rather than the spec's test_workers_page_marks_only_expired_workers). test_journeys.py has 10 test functions, against 8 on main.
issues.resolution: Add the three tests exactly as the spec's 'Write the page and API tests first' section describes. (a) In tests/test_journeys.py, add test_workers_page_marks_only_riverside_expired_worker(client): sign_in(client, RIVERSIDE_MANAGER), GET /workers, assert exactly one 'badge-expired' and that it is inside the row from id="worker-103" up to </tr>. (b) In tests/test_journeys.py, add test_registration_is_not_expired_on_its_expiry_day(manager, monkeypatch): monkeypatch.setenv('ROTA_TODAY', '2026-02-14'), assert 'badge-expired' is not in /workers, and assert '<option value="3">Chloe Martin</option>' is in /shifts. (c) In tests/test_api.py, add test_workers_api_shape_is_unchanged(manager): every worker from /api/workers has exactly the keys {id, name, role, employment, registration_number, registration_expires}. issues.description: The workers page does not follow the design the spec asked for. The spec wanted assignments.workers(scope, today) built on with_expiry(), with the template reading worker.expired. Instead, app.py:156-159 imports rules (app.py:24) and calls rules.registration_expired(data.to_rule_worker(...)) inline, then passes a separate `expired` id set to the template (templates/workers.html:17). So the 'add the expiry flag' logic lives in two places (here and assignments.with_expiry at assignments.py:36-38), and clock.today() is called once per worker row.
issues.resolution: Add `def workers(scope: Scope, today: date) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: return with_expiry(scope.workers(), today)` to assignments.py. In app.py, make workers() render `workers=assignments.workers(scope, clock.today())` and drop the `expired` set and the `import rules`. In templates/workers.html, use `{% if worker.expired %}`.

combined_verdict.summary: The change marks expired workers in two places. The workers page shows a red Expired badge (app.py:156-159, templates/workers.html:17, static/style.css:69-70). In the shifts-board dropdown an expired worker is labelled '(Expired)' and disabled (assignments.py:36-44, app.py:122-124, templates/shifts.html:26). rules.py, data.py, the JSON API and all protected paths are unchanged. The artefacts show the feature working: 04-expired-unavailable.png and keyframe session-04 show 'Chloe Martin (Expired)' greyed out in the #assign-8 list. 05-workers.png, 06-workers-expired-badge.png and keyframes 06-08 show the badge on Chloe Martin only. The final runs passed: e2e 9/9 steps, pytest 48 passed, isolation 16 passed. The change still cannot ship: three tests the spec requires as proof of its acceptance criteria were never written (the Riverside badge, the expiry-day edge case and the unchanged API shape). It also departs from the spec's design and leaves the README unchanged. | The change adds an "Expired" badge to the workers page (templates/workers.html:17, computed in app.py:155-159 with the existing rules.registration_expired). In the shifts board dropdown, an expired worker's option now reads "Name (Expired)" and is disabled (assignments.py:36-44, app.py:122-124, templates/shifts.html:26). rules.py, data.py, the API routes and every protected path are untouched. All five acceptance criteria from the issue are met. 04-expired-unavailable.png and keyframe session-04 show "Chloe Martin (Expired)" greyed out in the Wednesday night dropdown, with the other nurses still selectable. 05-workers.png, 06-workers-expired-badge.png and keyframes 06-08 show the red Expired badge on Chloe Martin's row only. Logs: pytest 48 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped; isolation 16 passed; e2e passed all 9 steps. The gaps against the detailed spec cost something later but do not break anything: some planned tests are missing, the README is not updated, and the workers route repeats the expiry check instead of using a helper in assignments.py.

issues.description: Three tests that the spec names as the proof for its acceptance criteria are missing. (1) tests/test_journeys.py::test_workers_page_marks_only_riverside_expired_worker (Riverside manager sees one badge, on worker-103) is not there. (2) tests/test_journeys.py::test_registration_is_not_expired_on_its_expiry_day (with ROTA_TODAY=2026-02-14 there is no badge and '<option value="3">Chloe Martin</option>' stays enabled) is not there; this is the only proof for the criterion 'On the expiry day itself, nothing is marked'. (3) tests/test_api.py::test_workers_api_shape_is_unchanged is not there; it was to prove that /api/workers keys are unchanged. Only two tests were added: tests/test_journeys.py:39-46 (dropdown) and tests/test_journeys.py:61-67 (Northfield badge, named test_workers_page_marks_expired_registrations rather than the spec's test_workers_page_marks_only_expired_workers). test_journeys.py has 10 test functions, against 8 on main.
issues.resolution: Add the three tests exactly as the spec's 'Write the page and API tests first' section describes. (a) In tests/test_journeys.py, add test_workers_page_marks_only_riverside_expired_worker(client): sign_in(client, RIVERSIDE_MANAGER), GET /workers, assert exactly one 'badge-expired' and that it is inside the row from id="worker-103" up to </tr>. (b) In tests/test_journeys.py, add test_registration_is_not_expired_on_its_expiry_day(manager, monkeypatch): monkeypatch.setenv('ROTA_TODAY', '2026-02-14'), assert 'badge-expired' is not in /workers, and assert '<option value="3">Chloe Martin</option>' is in /shifts. (c) In tests/test_api.py, add test_workers_api_shape_is_unchanged(manager): every worker from /api/workers has exactly the keys {id, name, role, employment, registration_number, registration_expires}. Optionally rename the Northfield badge test to test_workers_page_marks_only_expired_workers. Then re-run python -m pytest -q tests.

issues.description: The workers page does not follow the design the spec asked for. The spec wanted assignments.workers(scope, today) built on with_expiry(), with the template reading worker.expired. Instead, app.py:156-159 imports rules (app.py:24) and calls rules.registration_expired(data.to_rule_worker(...)) inline, then passes a separate `expired` id set to the template (templates/workers.html:17). So the 'add the expiry flag' logic lives in two places (here and assignments.with_expiry at assignments.py:36-38), and clock.today() is called once per worker row.
issues.resolution: Add `def workers(scope: Scope, today: date) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: return with_expiry(scope.workers(), today)` to assignments.py. In app.py, make workers() render `workers=assignments.workers(scope, clock.today())` and drop the `expired` set and the `import rules`. In templates/workers.html, use `{% if worker.expired %}`.
